items.question: What kind of worldly activity do deluded people continue to perform?
premises: People act in the same manner as before.
Their activity is produced by birth and death.
Their activity belongs to worldly existence.
items.inference: Deluded people persist in worldly activity driven by the cycle of birth and death.
items.plain_english: In the same way, they engage in worldly activity brought about by birth and death.

rows.grounds: object; the family or path of Kula

items.question: Why do people fail to embrace the liberating dharma of Kula?
premises: People do not resort to Kula.
Kula-dharma releases one from the bond of worldly becoming.
The liberating quality of Kula-dharma is not embraced.
items.inference: People do not take up the dharma of Kula that frees from the bondage of existence.
items.plain_english: They do not resort to the Kula dharma, which liberates from the bondage of worldly existence.

items.question: How do deluded humans address the Lady of Kula in their requests?
premises: Humans act out of delusion.
They make requests with affection.
They address the Lady of Kula.
items.inference: Deluded humans affectionately beg the Lady of Kula without true understanding.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Kula, out of delusion humans affectionately beg from you.

items.question: What other teachings do people pursue instead of Kula dharma?
premises: People act in the same deluded manner.
They turn to scriptures meant for bound beings.
Those scriptures yield fruits tied to the bondage of action.
items.inference: People pursue teachings that keep them bound by the results of action.
items.plain_english: In the same way, they turn to the scriptures of bound beings, which yield the fruits of bondage through action.

items.question: Why do people not inquire into the dharma of Kula?
premises: People do not ask about Kula-dharma.
Kula-dharma grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
They prefer other teachings instead.
items.inference: People neglect Kula-dharma despite its capacity to grant enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: They do not ask about the Kula dharma, which grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: What analogies illustrate the failure to recognize true value?
premises: Something made of sugar can be mistaken for gravel.
A jewel can be mistaken for glass.
Such mistakes arise from erroneous perception.
items.inference: People fail to recognize what is truly valuable due to mistaken perception.
items.plain_english: They mistake what is made of sugar for gravel, and a jewel for glass.

items.question: Why do people fail to recognize the Kaula way?
premises: People do not know the Kaula way.
Their ignorance is compared to mistaking valuable things for worthless ones.
They are deprived of the Goddess's grace.
items.inference: Without the Goddess's grace, people cannot recognize the Kaula way.
items.plain_english: Likewise, deprived of your grace, they do not recognize the Kaula way.

items.question: How powerful is ignorance in deluding beings, even divine ones?
premises: Ignorance is being questioned as a deluding force.
Even immortals are considered possible victims.
The Goddess is addressed as witness to this power.
items.inference: Ignorance is so powerful that it can delude even the immortals.
items.plain_english: O Lady of the gods, what then of ignorance—can it not delude even the immortals?

items.question: What conduct and goal are affirmed as truly to be pursued?
premises: A certain conduct is to be practiced and recited.
The supreme state is to be attained.
This is affirmed emphatically.
items.inference: The proper conduct leads to the attainment of the supreme state.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'caraṇaṃ' as conduct or footstep is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Thus indeed, this conduct is to be recited and practiced, and the supreme state is to be attained.

items.question: Who truly understands the path that grants enjoyment and liberation?
premises: Only the devotees of the Goddess know this.
Others do not know it.
What is known grants enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: True knowledge of the path granting enjoyment and liberation belongs only to the Goddess's devotees.
items.plain_english: Only your devotees know that which grants enjoyment and liberation, not others.

items.question: How does delusion perpetuate itself among people?
premises: Some people delude all others.
Those who delude are themselves previously deluded.
Delusion is transmitted from one to another.
items.inference: Those already deluded spread delusion to others.
items.plain_english: Having been deluded before, they themselves delude all people.

items.question: What is the relationship between a deluded master and his followers?
premises: The nature of the master is questioned.
The servants are said to be of the same kind.
The condition of followers reflects the condition of the leader.
items.inference: If the master is of a certain deluded nature, the servants will be of the same nature.

items.plain_english: What kind of master would he be? The servants would be of the same kind.
